topics.topic: Recorded outcome when trial or admission value output exceeds stored_value_bytes_max
questions: What outcome and records result when a trial or admission execution returns a value above `stored_value_bytes_max` but within the contract's `output_bytes` bound?

When a trial or admission execution otherwise succeeds but a value output exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, what outcome and detail are recorded, given that the output cannot be stored as the StoredValue required by M07?

quotes: execute_trial_case: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is the sandbox outcome of the same name; a succeeded execution is passed when the case has no expected outputs or every output's digest equals the expected one, a many file output equal only with the same length and equal digests position by position, and output_mismatch otherwise; a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant makes the outcome contract_violation.

execute_trial_case: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] For passed and output_mismatch the outputs are recorded, a value as a StoredValue stored with put_value_bytes and a file by digest, size and media type only as a FileFactsRef whose disclosure_class is the highest class of the case's inputs, every output taking that class; other outcomes record outputs None; one RecordTrialExecutionChange is written through record_change with resources_used, the sandbox's detail_code (value_too_large for an output over the stored value ceiling), the sandbox's failure_detail, executed_at from kernel_now and the given actor.

admit_implementation: [BEHAVIOR] Acts as the kernel actor; when a verdict over the current corpus digest exists for the implementation it is reused and no case executes; otherwise every case of the corpus executes in corpus order through execute_trial_case, never stopping early on a failing case, and one RecordAdmissionVerdictChange records the trial execution ids in corpus order, verdict admitted exactly when the corpus is non-empty and every case passed, otherwise refused with an EmptyCorpusRefusal or a FailingCaseRefusal naming the first case in corpus order that did not pass and its outcome.
judgement.why: State 7 specifies a contract_violation TrialExecution with detail value_too_large and no outputs; during admission that non-passing case contributes to a refused verdict.

topics.topic: Scope of A08 rule 5 startup manifest validation without operation or proposed ports
questions: Which A08 rule 5 checks run at startup, given that several require a particular operation and proposed ports but startup names neither?

Which A08 rule 5 checks are performed at startup when no operation name or proposed ports exist, and are they applied to every capability or only to the manifest structure needed to inspect the selected instance?

judgement.why: This asks the same startup manifest-validation scope question as P1, and neither the relevant State 4 passage nor the deciding later text has changed.

precedent.topic: Exact manifest checks and capability scope of check_installed_instances at startup without operation or proposed-port context
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: State 6 notes limit startup validation to read_service_record’s five record-level checks and the specified credential-header collision checks, excluding operation- and proposal-specific validation.

topics.topic: Persistence and masking location for bounded trial execution failure detail
questions: Where is a trial execution's bounded failure detail persisted so later trial evidence and the repair view can return and mask it?
